newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds tumble on profit-taking after Dublin.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds tumble on profit-taking after Dublin.

text.p: Bunds posted one of their biggest declines of the month on Monday after a bout of profit taking following last week's gains was given added urgency by worries about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
The December DTB Bund future was down 27 basis points in late trade to 97.99, but well off its low for the day of 97.88.

Traders said profit-taking in the Bund market started after the Ecofin meeting in Dublin over the weekend failed to give non-core European bond markets reason to continue last week's advance, starting a multi-national pull back that carried Bunds lower.
"Bunds had gained a lot last week along with other European markets on speculation about the Dublin summit and quickly fell on profit taking," said Timo Klein, analyst at MMS International.
Pro-monetary union comments such as those heard in Dublin are normally viewed as bad for the Bund market, which analysts fear has the most to lose from a single European currency.
Other European markets, meanwhile, did not see enough concrete progress toward monetary union to continue their advance from last week.
Bunds also were hurt by reports of Yeltsin's fragile health, stirring worries about political instability in Russia.
Traders now look for Bunds to trade in a narrow range ahead of Tuesday's Federal Reserve Board meeting and the first of four German state consumer price reports which are due from Tuesday.

Assuming the Fed only raises rates marginally at the meeting, Bunds should continue to outperorm T-notes likely driving the yield spread to around 90 basis points from the current 78 basis points, traders said.
